label: Field
description: Places one field of the view's entity on the page and renders it with the component of its field type (a select for single_select, a user picker for user, and so on). The field's definition — type, label, constraints, choice list — comes from the entity; the placement only decides where the field appears and how it is presented on this view. Rule hooks (required, visible, read-only, options, value, message) and field permissions apply automatically.
usage: Bind field to an existing field key of the view's entity; never invent a key — add the field to the entity first.
Leave label empty to use the field's own label; override only when this view needs different wording.
Use emphasis: large for the one or two values a reader scans for first (e.g. title on a form).
Use readOnly for presentation only; to stop people editing, change field permissions or add a data-scoped read_only rule.
constraints: field must be a key of the view's entity; deprecated fields cannot be newly placed.
A field may be placed at most once per view.
readOnly is presentational and never a security control; every write is authorized by field permissions on the server.
Fields the viewer may not read are not sent to the client at all — not as values, labels, or placeholders.
System fields (auto_number, platform timestamps) always render read-only.

field.description: Field key of the view's entity, e.g. assignee or tenant__vendor.

helpText.description: Helper text under the input; defaults to the field's help.

readOnly.description: Form-level read-only. Never a security control.

binding.description: Two-way binding to record.<field>; the value has the shape of the field type's valueSchema.

accessibility.keyboard: Tab moves between fields; type-specific keys apply (see field.<type>). Esc reverts an inline edit, Enter commits.
accessibility.notes: The control's role comes from the field type. The label (or override) is the accessible name; helpText and validation messages are linked with aria-describedby; required state uses aria-required.

responsive: Label above the value in narrow cells and below 720px; label beside the value in wide two-column cards on desktop.
